output.name: Sokul

anatomy.part: breast, the middle of the body
right wing elbow, the bright shoulder joint

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went off like a sail torn from its mast, and Tavo laughed so hard the cliffs rang. A gull named Sokul was working the north ledges that morning with a cod in its beak. It saw the sky leaving and went after it, higher than any gull had flown. Tavo took the bird by one wingtip and bent it back, and Sokul had to stoop to come home, and it came home with the fish still in its beak. Hesk counted the wing. Ennu says the bend is why the gulls ride the wind so close to the cliffs, always testing it. The Gulls, who carry word between Vel and the islands, say Sokul is still aloft, and that when its bent wing points at the house, someone will fly back. Mend your own tears with sinew. Watch the gull's wing before you fly.
output.verse:
One bent wing bends back
the gull stoops low to the cliff
Hesk counts each wing home

problems: Head and crown stars (69713, 69483) nearly coincide at the top of the body, so the head reads as one point instead of a head with a crown.
Beak tip (70497) sits well out to the left of the head, which reads acceptably as a beak, but the beak is a single point with no shape.

Labels collide: 'right wing elbow, the bright shoulder joint' overprints 'right wingtip' near (400-510, 205-215), and 'breast, the middle of the body' is cut off at the frame edge ('the middle of the bo').

Wings are asymmetric: the left wing reaches about 190 px from the body to wingtip 73695 at (102, 246), while the right wing reaches only about 50 px from elbow 67301 at (396, 218) to wingtip 66234 at (447, 219). The right wing looks truncated.
The pose is an upright, spread-wing bird rather than a stooping (diving) gull. Wings are nearly horizontal and the body is not angled downward, so the title's 'stooping' is not shown.
Tail fan (69038) at about (323, 349) is a small lobed shape; the forked read in the guess is only weakly suggested.
An unlabelled bright star at about (84, 416) sits outside the figure and is not a key star; it is harmless but may confuse readers.
Figure is the right way up (head at top, tail at bottom) and the outline is a real silhouette with wing and body contours, not just the gold skeleton lines.
judge.advice: Keep as is for this round; the figure passes the thresholds (match 4, fit 3). Optional improvements if a redraw happens later: (1) separate the head and crown stars by about 8-10 px so the head has a visible top; (2) lengthen the right wing so wingtip 66234 sits near x≈480-500 with elbow 67301 at (396, 218) remaining the shoulder; (3) move the 'breast' label to the right or shorten it so it stays inside the frame; (4) angle the whole body about 20-30 degrees downward toward the tail to show the stoop; (5) make the tail fan a clearer fork by placing 69038 at the centre of a V with two lobes near (340, 355) and (310, 355).

guess: A bird in flight with outstretched wings, seen from the front or back, with a forked tail
